title: Embrace Faith & Fresh Start
subtitle: Day 0-1
description: This stage is about protecting the first moments after Shahada: faith, calm, purification, and one or two trusted next steps. You do not need to rebuild your entire life in a day.
mainGoal: Understand your Shahada, take care of the first 24 hours, and perform Ghusl when you are ready.
success: You know you are Muslim, you have a simple next step, and you are not pressuring yourself to learn everything at once.
dontWorry: Do not worry about memorizing long prayers right now.
Do not worry about changing your name; it is not required.
Do not worry about announcing everything immediately.
Do not worry about knowing every rule; learning is gradual.
focusNow: Hold onto the meaning of the Shahada.
Make Ghusl when you can do it calmly.
Choose one trusted person or masjid to contact.
canWait: Changing your name, wardrobe, or whole routine overnight.
Explaining Islam to everyone in your life.
askHelpIf: You are not sure how to do Ghusl.
You need a witness, certificate, or local community connection.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I talk to family?

title: Building Foundations
subtitle: Week 1
description: This week focuses on gentle practice: learning the shape of prayer, visiting or contacting a masjid, and adding simple remembrance without shame or panic.
mainGoal: Begin a realistic prayer on-ramp and make a first connection with Muslim community.
success: You are attempting prayer in some form and you know where to ask for local help.
dontWorry: Do not worry about perfect Arabic pronunciation.
Do not worry if you miss prayers while learning.
Do not worry about fitting in at the masjid right away.
Do not worry about doing every optional practice.
focusNow: Learn the prayer times and basic movements.
Find one masjid or mentor you can ask questions.
Use short dua and dhikr to keep your heart connected.
canWait: Optional prayers and detailed differences of opinion.
askHelpIf: You are confused about prayer basics.
You feel nervous entering a masjid.
Work or school makes prayer timing difficult.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I visit a masjid?
How do I build prayer slowly?

title: Strengthening Practice
subtitle: Weeks 2-4
description: You are beginning to settle. This stage adds Quran, family conversations, and healthy ways to handle doubts or questions without overload.
mainGoal: Start a Quran habit, prepare for family and friend conversations, and learn how to ask good questions.
success: You have a small Quran routine, one or two gentle scripts for people close to you, and a healthier way to handle doubts.
dontWorry: Do not worry about reading Arabic fluently.
Do not worry about understanding every verse.
Do not worry if faith feels up and down.
Do not worry about winning arguments.
focusNow: Listen to or read a little Quran regularly.
Choose who needs to know about your Islam and when.
Bring difficult questions to reliable people.
askHelpIf: Family pressure becomes unsafe or controlling.
Doubts are making you unable to function.
You cannot tell which sources are reliable.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I protect family ties?

title: Broadening Practice
subtitle: Months 2-3
description: This stage helps Islam enter daily life through food choices, fasting preparation, modesty, and practical boundaries at a pace you can actually sustain.
mainGoal: Understand halal basics, prepare for fasting, and approach modesty as gradual growth rather than panic.
success: You can make basic food choices, you understand fasting at a beginner level, and you know which lifestyle questions need local guidance.
dontWorry: Do not overhaul your entire pantry overnight.
Do not treat every ingredient question as an emergency.
Do not compare your clothing journey to someone else's.
Do not take fasting hardship questions from random online comments.
focusNow: Avoid clear haram foods and build confidence with simple halal choices.
Learn fasting basics before Ramadan or your first voluntary fast.
Take modesty changes one sustainable step at a time.
askHelpIf: Food or clothing pressure is harming your family safety.
A medical condition may affect fasting.
You need rulings about work, school, or financial details.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I eat halal practically?

title: Deepening Faith
subtitle: Months 4-6
description: Practice is becoming more familiar. This stage focuses on character, reliable learning, and asking better questions so your growth stays grounded and calm.
mainGoal: Develop Islamic character, learn how to ask qualified people, and build a steady knowledge path.
success: You notice better character in daily life and you have a clearer path for learning without overload.
dontWorry: Do not worry about becoming a scholar.
Do not worry about knowing every opinion.
Do not worry if questions still come up.
Do not make Islam feel like constant self-criticism.
focusNow: Practice honesty, patience, prayer, and good manners.
Learn how to phrase personal questions clearly.
Choose one steady class, teacher, or book.
canWait: Trying to follow every speaker online.
askHelpIf: You receive conflicting answers and feel stuck.
A ruling affects family, marriage, work, or money.
Your community experience feels pressuring or unhealthy.

goodNextQuestions.label: How do I ask good questions?

title: Lifelong Growth
subtitle: Beyond 6 Months
description: Islam is a lifelong path. This stage introduces bigger future responsibilities, like zakat and Hajj, while keeping your learning sustainable.
mainGoal: Understand future pillars and continue learning with qualified guidance.
success: You know that zakat and Hajj are serious responsibilities when conditions apply, and you know to seek qualified review for personal cases.
dontWorry: Do not worry about Hajj before you are able.
Do not worry about zakat if you do not meet the threshold.
Do not worry about finishing the whole religion; growth continues for life.
focusNow: Learn the big picture of zakat and Hajj.
Stay connected to trustworthy teachers and community.
canWait: Detailed personal zakat calculations without financial review.
Hajj planning before you are financially and physically able.
Advanced specialization unless you are ready.
askHelpIf: You think zakat may now apply to you.
You are planning Hajj or Umrah.
You need financial or legal-adjacent guidance.
